title.en: Gadol Hashem: no investigating His greatness

summary.en: After a few words on the nusach of tefillah set by the Anshei Knesses Hagedolah, the Mashgiach takes up the verse 'Gadol Hashem… v'ligdulaso ein cheker'. He explains that each sense grasps its own kind of thing, a picture with the eyes and a symphony with the ears, and that the intellect is not the faculty for grasping Hashem.

title.en: The neshamah and the ruach hakodesh of Klal Yisroel

summary.en: Citing the Kuzari, the Mashgiach explains that every Jew has a neshamah and a measure of ruach hakodesh, and only sin insulates him from it; the neshamah knows what lies beyond walls and time. Klal Yisroel as a whole has ruach hakodesh, which is why its minhagim are true, as he shows from the Binas Adam and a teshuvah of Rav Moshe Feinstein.

title.en: The mind cannot reach Hashem; emunah through Torah and mitzvos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the human mind was made for the physical world and breaks down on questions of infinite time and space; Hashem is felt through Torah, mitzvos and kedushah. He discusses the old dispute over chakirah, says that today one should not engage in it, and stresses that the Torah never proves its ikkarim by investigation, unlike religions that believe 'because he said so'.

title.en: A whole nation saw: the mesorah of Sinai

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the pesukim in Devarim that no nation ever heard Hashem speak from the fire, and explains that something an entire people witnessed and handed down cannot be denied. He reads a teshuvah of the Yismach Moshe on doubts in emunah, compares denial of Sinai to denying the Holocaust or Julius Caesar, and explains that the nations too accept the Torah's miracles.

title.en: Dor l'dor: the tzaddikim as Hashem's handiwork

summary.en: Returning to the verse, the Mashgiach explains that Hashem's greatness is known not through philosophy but through the mesorah, 'dor l'dor yeshabach ma'asecha', and warns that every Jew must guard his emunah. He brings the Zohar on Shavuos night that 'ma'asecha' and 'ma'aseh yadav' are the tzaddikim, and describes Jews whose avodah radiates onto others.

title.en: Lechovitch, Belz and the Satmar Rav's megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how a poritz listening to the Lechovitcher daven said that his love for his wife was nothing next to the Jew's love for Hashem, and how the young R' Shalom of Belz told the megillah in Lublin. He describes hearing the Satmar Rav read the megillah for two hours, brings the Chasam Sofer and Kedushas Levi on the light of the megillah, and his shout at 'hakerovim v'harechokim'.

title.en: The falling generations, and what later generations understand

summary.en: With the example of a falling stone that speeds up as it drops, the Mashgiach explains that the decline between generations grows ever greater, so earlier tzaddikim are beyond compare. Then, with other meforshim, he reads 'dor l'dor' as later generations understanding what Hashem did, bringing the Chazon Ish's mashal of the tailor cutting silk after the destruction in Europe.

title.en: Hadar kevod hodecha: the beauty of creation

summary.en: On 'hadar kevod hodecha', the Mashgiach describes the beauty of the countryside that the city hides, and explains 'hazan es ha'olam… b'chen' : Hashem could have fed people like a car with fuel, but made food beautiful, varied and tasty, for which one must thank and praise Him. He ends with the ever-changing clouds and his love of speaking about Hashem's wonders.

catalogTitle: ועזוז נוראותיך

oneLiner.en: Learning the verses of Ashrei from 'Ve'ezuz nora'osecha' onward, the Mashgiach explains that Dovid HaMelech sees Hashem's mercy and hashgachah in every small thing, and that a person who believes this can turn suffering into delight.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach learns Tehillim 145 verse by verse. Others speak of Hashem's might when something extraordinary happens, but Dovid HaMelech sees His greatness in a leaf or a feather, and a small act done for avodas Hashem counts more in Heaven than events that make history. Hashem is gracious and slow to anger: He waits for the wicked and even gives them strength, hoping they will return. His mercy is on all His creatures, shown in stories of Rebbi and the calf, the Arizal and the chickens, and the Ba'al Shem Tov and the worm. The Mashgiach explains the great destruction fifty years earlier as Hashem gathering damaged souls for their tikkun, like leftovers mixed into a kugel, and tells stories of the Malach, the Sadigura Rebbe and the Beis Aharon showing that everything has a reckoning. Whoever believes in hashgachah pratis sweetens his suffering: nega becomes oneg, as on Shabbos. He ends with 'Yoducha' and the levels of tzaddikim and chassidim.

en: Dovid HaMelech does not need wonders to see Hashem; he sees His greatness and His connection to every small thing in the world.
Hashem's patience goes beyond waiting: He keeps giving the sinner life and strength, even to keep sinning, so that he may still do teshuvah.
Hashem's mercy extends to every creature, down to a single worm, and every Jew must know that all He does is with mercy and kindness.
Everything that happens to a person has an exact reckoning, often a tikkun of a former life, which no human calculation can grasp.
A person who recognizes that his suffering comes from Hashem through hashgachah pratis sweetens the judgments, so that the greatest suffering can shrink to a trifle.
The same letters can turn nega (affliction) into oneg (delight), and this is the secret of Shabbos, on which a Jew testifies that Hashem created everything.

title.en: Seeing Hashem in every small thing

summary.en: On 'Ve'ezuz nora'osecha' and 'Zecher rav tuvcha', the Mashgiach explains that others praise Hashem when something awesome happens, but Dovid HaMelech sees Him in a leaf or a feather. A bottle of milk bought to daven better makes a greater impression in Heaven than events that make the newspapers.

title.en: Gracious, slow to anger and great in kindness

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the wicked prosper while tzaddikim are judged to a hair's breadth: Hashem waits for teshuvah. Beyond that, as 'great in kindness', He even gives the sinner strength to continue, as if handing more stones to someone throwing stones at Him.

title.en: His mercy is on all His creatures

summary.en: On 'Tov Hashem lakol', the Mashgiach tells of Rebbi and the calf, the Arizal and the chickens, and the Ba'al Shem Tov and the worm in the heat, showing that Hashem has mercy on every creature, and says every Jew must know that all He does is with mercy.

title.en: The destruction and the kugel of souls

summary.en: The Mashgiach addresses the great destruction of Klal Yisrael fifty years earlier: Hashem gathers souls from the generations of the Flood and the Dispersion into one generation before Moshiach, like a housewife mixing Shabbos leftovers into a kugel, and their suffering is a light judgment compared to what they deserved.

title.en: The Malach and the two neighbors

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of two neighbors who came to the Malach, one with a bad wife and one with poor parnassah. Through the verse in Iyov about three chances, he explains that such a hard life lets a soul return to the world for its tikkun.

title.en: The mezuzah in Sadigura and the Beis Aharon

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a chassid whom the Sadigura Rebbe kept from moving, who died after affixing his mezuzah with kavanah, and of a man whose wife tormented him, whom the Beis Aharon sent home, after which he suffered in the street instead. Both show that everything comes with a reckoning.

title.en: Believing sweetens the suffering

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara's measure of suffering, a nickel instead of a quarter, and the Bnei Yissaschar: one who acknowledges that suffering comes from Hashem turns great suffering into a trifle. He explains that nega becomes oneg through the letters, and that one should daven for the judgments to be sweetened for himself, his family and all Yisrael.

title.en: The metzora's nega and the oneg of Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads 'the nega did not turn its ayin' as the nega not becoming oneg, and explains that Shabbos, on which a Jew testifies that Hashem created everything, is the secret of turning nega into oneg and pesha into shefa.

title.en: Yoducha: Your works and Your chassidim

summary.en: On 'Yoducha Hashem kol ma'asecha', the Mashgiach explains that the soul praises Hashem with every breath, that tzaddikim are called His 'handiwork' and adorn the Torah on Shavuos night, and that chassidim are a higher level who bring blessing into the Shechinah. He closes by announcing a break to learn about Pesach.

catalogTitle: כבוד מלכותך

oneLiner.en: Through the pesukim of Ashrei from 'vachasidecha yevarchucha' to 'somech Hashem', the Mashgiach explains how Klal Yisroel blesses Hashem, why Hashem's rule over each generation differs, and why today's generation is tested above all in emunah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach explains that all of creation praises Hashem by its very existence, but only Klal Yisroel, the 'chasidim' of the world, can bless Him: their mitzvos and brachos bring strength and shefa (flow of blessing) into the upper worlds, as Rabbi Yishmael was asked to bless Hashem in the Kodesh HaKodashim. Such a blessing must follow the fixed nusach of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, with Hashem's name and His kingship, which is the meaning of 'kevod malchuscha yomeru'. Yet all the praises only make His might known to people. 'Malchuscha' speaks of space, 'memshalt'cha' of time: in each generation Hashem rules with a different purpose, and the task of this generation is emunah. The Mashgiach describes a world stripped of kingship and of fear, set up so that believing is hard, and brings stories about the fear of a king. Emunah is drawn from Yetzias Mitzrayim, which Hashem showed once and which is handed down. He ends with the missing nun of Ashrei and 'somech Hashem'.

en: All creatures praise Hashem by existing, but only the Jewish people, the 'chasidim' among the nations, can bless Him and bring shefa into all the worlds through their mitzvos and brachos.

Because a Jew's blessing opens the upper worlds, it must follow the nusach of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, where every word is weighed by pshat, remez, drush and sod, and it needs Hashem's name and His kingship.
All the praises of Hashem only make His might known to people as far as they can grasp; no person, angel or seraph can reach the end of His praise.
'Malchuscha' is Hashem's kingship across all worlds, in space; 'memshalt'cha' is His governance in time, which changes from generation to generation according to each generation's tikkun.
The task of the present generation, before Moshiach, is emunah, and the world is deliberately set up without kingship or fear so that believing will be a real test.
Emunah is drawn from Yetzias Mitzrayim, which the whole people saw; Hashem showed it once and does not repeat it for every generation, and it is handed down by mesorah.

title.en: Only Klal Yisroel can bless Hashem

summary.en: On 'yoducha Hashem kol maasecha vachasidecha yevarchucha', the Mashgiach explains that all creation praises Hashem by existing, while the Jewish people, the 'chasidim' among the nations, bless Him and bring shefa into the worlds, like Rabbi Yishmael who was asked to bless Hashem in the Kodesh HaKodashim.

title.en: Kevod malchuscha: the fixed nusach of a brachah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a Jew's praise opens the upper worlds, so after prophecy ended the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah fixed a nusach in which every word is measured. A brachah needs Hashem's name and kingship, and this is 'kevod malchuscha yomeru'; he brings Tosafos on how Shemoneh Esrei has malchus.

title.en: Praise only to make His might known

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains 'lehodia livnei ha'adam gevurosav': all the praises fixed by the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah and David HaMelech cannot reach the end of Hashem's praise, and only show people His might as far as they can grasp. He calls the pasuk a parenthesis in the middle of the alef-beis of Ashrei.

title.en: Malchus in space, memshalah in time

summary.en: On 'malchuscha malchus kol olamim umemshalt'cha bechol dor vador', the Mashgiach distinguishes a king from a ruler, as with Yosef in Mitzrayim, and explains that kingship speaks of space while governance speaks of time. Each generation has its own task, and the task of today's generation is emunah.

title.en: A generation tested in emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chofetz Chaim that before Moshiach the test is emunah, and the uncensored Rambam that even the founder of Christianity prepared the world for the idea of Moshiach. He tells of the Ba'al Shem Tov leaving a wagon driver who did not cross himself, explains that heresy is worse than idolatry, and describes a world without fear of kingship.

title.en: Fear of a king, then and now

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a chassid of the Ba'al HaTanya who learned how to daven from a soldier flogged for frozen ears, and of Czar Nikolai's old soldier whose service warmed his blood. He explains that people once feared a king and so feared the Day of Judgment, while today there is no kingship and no religion, so that the Jews' emunah will be tested.

title.en: Each generation adds its part; the tzaddik rules

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rav Samson Raphael Hirsch that each generation contributes something whose purpose is seen only generations later, when Hashem's hand as captain becomes clear. From Chassidic sefarim he adds that 'memshalt'cha' is the tzaddik who rules through fear of Heaven, found in every generation.

title.en: Emunah from Yetzias Mitzrayim; somech Hashem

summary.en: In the days of Sefirah the Mashgiach explains that emunah is drawn from Yetzias Mitzrayim, where the ten makos matched the ten maamaros and led to the ten dibros. He tells of Reb Elchonon Wasserman and a musician's 'concert' to explain why Hashem does not repeat miracles for every generation, then explains why the nun is missing in Ashrei and 'somech Hashem' comes first.
